q: 1. The explosive for blasting is usually expressed in terms of
options: volume of earthwork that can be blasted
explain: Explosives used for blasting are quantified and paid for by their weight, expressed in kilograms.

q: 2. The unit of measurement of pile driving is
explain: Pile driving is paid based on the length of pile driven into the ground, hence measured per metre (or per running metre of pile).

q: 3. The unit of measurement of lintel over opening is
explain: A lintel is a solid RCC/masonry member with length, width and depth, so its quantity is measured by volume, m³.

q: 4. The quantity for expansion joint in buildings is worked out in
explain: Expansion joints are linear features running along the length of a structure, so their quantity is measured in running meters.

q: 5. The quantity of cement concrete PCC having thickness less than 75mm is normally measured in
explain: Thin layers of PCC (below 75mm) are measured by area (m^2) instead of volume.

q: 6. The volume of cement required for 10 m3 of brickwork in 1:6 cement mortar is approximately equal to
explain: For 10 m3 of brickwork with about 30% mortar volume in a 1:6 mix, the cement content works out to approximately 3/7 m3 as per standard rate-analysis calculations.

q: 7. Whenever the whitewashing or distempering is done on corrugated iron sheets, in the estimation the plan area of that sheet is increased by
explain: Because corrugations add extra surface area beyond the flat plan area, whitewashing/distempering quantities on corrugated iron sheets are increased by 14% over plan area.

q: 8. Compute the amount of cement required for 10 m^3 RCC having M20 (1:1.5:3).
explain: All options are mathematically equivalent for this mix ratio once converted between volume, bags, and weight.

q: 9. The c/s area (mm^2) and unit weight (kg/m) of 16 mm steel bar is respectively
explain: Area = πr² = 201 mm². Unit weight = D²/162 = 16²/162 ≈ 1.58 kg/m.

q: 10. The amount of cement required for 1 m^3 mortar (1:6) plaster
explain: Using standard shrinkage and wastage factors for 1:6 mortar, the cement required is roughly 265 kg.

q: 11. The chamber provided in long horizontal members to counteract the effects of deflection is
explain: To counteract anticipated deflection, long horizontal RCC members (like beams) are given an upward camber of about 1 in 250 of the span during construction.

q: 12. The brick work is measured in sq meter, in case of
options: Half brick walls or the partition
explain: All these items — honeycomb brickwork, brick flat soling, and half-brick walls/partitions — being thin or grid-type work, are measured by area (sq. m).

q: 13. The unit of measurement of brick work in flat soiling is
explain: Flat soling (a single layer of bricks laid flat on their face, e.g. below foundations) covers an area with negligible thickness variation, so it is measured in m².

q: 14. During the calculation of RCC the amount of steel deducted is
explain: In standard concrete volume calculations, the volume of steel reinforcement is not deducted.

q: 15. One hectare –meter represents a volume of
explain: 1 Hectare (10,000 m^2) x 1 meter depth = 10,000 m^3.

q: 16. The weight of 10 mm diameter mild steel rod per meter length is equal to
explain: Weight = D²/162 = 100/162 ≈ 0.617 kg/m, rounded to 0.62.

q: 17. If B is the width of formation, d is the height of the embankment, side slope S:1, for a highway with no transverse slope, the area of cross-section is
explain: For a simple trapezoidal embankment cross-section with formation width B, height d, and side slope S:1, the area works out to Bd + Sd^2, combining the rectangular and triangular side portions.

q: 18. Pick up the excavation where measurement is made in square meters for payment
options: surface dressing up to 15 cm depths
Surface excavation up to 30 cm depths
both of above b. and c.
explain: Both surface dressing (up to 15 cm) and surface excavation (up to 30 cm) are shallow, area-type earthwork items and are measured/paid for in square meters.

q: 19. While estimating for plastering, usually no deduction is made for
explain: In plastering quantity calculations, minor items like ends of beams, ends of rafters, and small openings up to 0.5 sq. m are conventionally not deducted, since the extra plaster around them roughly compensates.

q: 20. In the estimation of plastering surface the deductions are not made for
explain: Ends of structural members and very small openings are not deducted from total plastering area measurements.

q: 21. In the case of roof truss made of steel, rivets, bolts, nuts etc. normally account for
explain: An additional 5% weight is usually added to the main steel sections to account for connections like rivets and bolts.

q: 22. The unit of measurement of turfing in embankment is called
explain: Turfing (laying grass sod on embankment slopes) is a surface-covering activity, so it is measured by area, square metres.

q: 23. Approximate weight of 1 cubic meter of sand is
explain: The bulk density of dry sand typically ranges between 1500 kg/m³ and 1700 kg/m³. 1600 kg is the standard average used.

q: 24. The unit of payment for road side brick edging is in
explain: Roadside brick edging is a border item and is measured and paid for in square meters per the standard answer key.

q: 25. The following item of earth work is not measured separately
explain: Dead men (small unexcavated earth pillars left temporarily to check excavation levels) are a working aid and are not measured or paid for separately, since they get removed as part of the main excavation.

q: 26. The excavation exceeding 1.5 m in width and 10 sq. m in plan area with a depth not exceeding 30 cm, is termed as
explain: When excavation exceeds 1.5 m width and 10 sq. m plan area but the depth is limited to 30 cm, it is classified specifically as 'surface excavation' rather than ordinary deep excavation.

q: 27. The quantity of earth wok in 1 Km length of road following given section should be
explain: The cross-section is a triangle with base 6m and height 5m. Area = 0.5 * 6 * 5 = 15 m². For 1 km (1000m) length, Volume = 15 * 1000 = 15,000 m³.

q: 28. The normal lead and lift for earthwork in road construction are taken, respectively, as
explain: The standard normal lead and lift for earthwork disposal in road construction, as in general estimating practice, is 30 m and 1.5 m respectively.

q: 29. When not specified, the volume of steel in RCC works is taken as
explain: When reinforcement details are not specified, the steel content in RCC work is conventionally assumed to be about 0.6% to 1% of the concrete volume.

q: 30. The number of bricks required for a wall of 80 feet long 1 feet 3 inch thick and 7 feet high with one mortar joint is: (the dimension of brick is 10 inch by 5 inch by 3 inch)
explain: Wall volume = 80' * 1.25' * 7' = 700 cu.ft. Using standard brickwork norms (approx 14-15 bricks per cu.ft), the count is ~10,000.

q: 31. Working out the exact quantities of various item of work is known as
explain: Quantity surveying is the specific process of calculating exact quantities of materials and work items from project drawings.

q: 32. While mixing cement mortar by volume, the volume of a cement bag is specified as
explain: For volumetric mixing purposes, one bag of cement (50 kg) is taken to occupy a specified volume of 0.050 cu m (50 litres).

q: 33. For 100 sq. m cement concrete (1:2:4) 4 cm thick floor, the quantity of cement required, is 54% for concrete +10% for floor finishing.
explain: Using the standard cement content calculation (54% for concrete plus 10% additional for floor finishing) applied to the given floor volume, cement required works out to 0.94 m3.

q: 34. In case of steel rolling shutters, for the estimation of painted area, the plain area is multiplied by
explain: For steel rolling shutters, the plain (flat) area is taken as-is (multiplied by 1) for estimating the painted surface area.

q: 35. Number of bricks usually carried by a truck is
explain: A standard (ordinary) truck is conventionally assumed to carry about 2000 bricks per trip, per typical rate analysis norms.

q: 36. Number of bricks that can be carried by 8 tonner truck is
explain: An 8-tonne capacity truck, being larger than the ordinary truck, can carry approximately 3500 bricks per trip.
